title: One Step of the Game of Life

concept.title: Compute the new grid from the old one
body: In the Game of Life every cell is alive (1) or dead (0) and has up to 8 neighbours. All cells change **at the same time** depending on the old grid. So write the results into a second grid, never into the one you are still reading.

Check the borders before reading a neighbour: cells outside the grid count as dead. The rules: a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours stays alive, otherwise it dies; a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours becomes alive.

statement: A grid with `n` rows and `m` columns contains 1 (alive) and 0 (dead). Compute the next generation. A live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours stays alive, other live cells die. A dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours becomes alive. Neighbours are the 8 surrounding cells; cells outside the grid are dead. Print the new grid.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` numbers (0 or 1) each.
outputFormat: Print the next generation, `n` lines with `m` numbers each.

examples.note: A vertical bar of three cells becomes a horizontal bar.

hints: Never modify the grid you are reading; build a new one.
Count the live cells among the 8 neighbours, skipping the ones outside the grid.
Apply the rules to decide the new value of each cell.

solution.complexity: Time O(8 * n * m), space O(1) besides the output.
